description: Hi! I'm Sofia, a software developer (C#/.NET, Blazor, 5 years). I'd like to build a working web app for astronaut health on long missions, focused on what the crew can do when Earth is minutes away. I'm looking for: a designer (UI/slides), someone good at presenting/storytelling, and anyone who likes space science or health data. Beginners welcome! We'll work in Greek or English.
summary:
SpaceDermApp is an offline "second opinion" assistant for the crew doctor on a long mission to Mars. It focuses on skin problems, one of the most common medical issues reported on the International Space Station. The doctor adds a photo and describes what they see. A small open-source AI (Llama 3.2 1B) that runs entirely in the browser, with no internet, then suggests possible causes, questions to ask the crew member, what to check and warning signs to watch for. The doctor always decides: the app offers ideas, never a diagnosis.

It addresses the challenge's need for health software that works far from Earth. On the way to Mars a message takes 3 to 22 minutes one way, and contact can be lost completely, so the crew cannot always wait for help from the ground. Our app answers in seconds, 24/7, on an ordinary laptop, and health data never leaves the device. It shows that a small offline AI can support crew medical autonomy, and the same idea could help people on Earth who are far from a doctor.
details:
LINKS

- Live app: https://doumsof99.github.io/SpaceDermApp (needs a WebGPU browser such as Chrome or Edge; the first start downloads the AI model once, then it works offline)

- Code: https://github.com/DoumSof99/SpaceDermApp

WHAT IT DOES

SpaceDermApp is a "second opinion" tool for the crew doctor on a long mission to Mars. It focuses on skin problems, one of the most common medical issues on the ISS. The doctor adds a photo of the skin problem and describes what they see. A small AI that runs fully offline in the browser then suggests possible causes, questions to ask the crew member, what to check or watch, and warning signs. The doctor always decides: the app gives ideas, never a diagnosis.

HOW IT WORKS

- It is a web app (Blazor WebAssembly) that runs entirely in the browser. It is hosted as static files on GitHub Pages, with no server behind it.

- On first start it downloads a free, open-source language model (Llama 3.2 1B Instruct, 4-bit) through WebLLM and keeps it in the browser cache. After that it runs on the device's graphics card (WebGPU) with no internet at all.

- The doctor adds a photo, which stays next to the case for review, and types a description. The AI does not analyse the photo yet; it works from the doctor's description.

- The AI gets background facts from NASA and medical research: rashes are common on the ISS, skin gets thinner and heals more slowly in space, and sweat does not drip in microgravity. It must answer in a fixed format with four headings, list at most 3 causes, give no medicine doses and stay under 220 words.

- The answer appears word by word. Quick follow-up buttons let the doctor ask, for example, "Which signs mean I should contact Earth?"

BENEFITS

- Works when Earth is far away: on a Mars mission a message takes 3 to 22 minutes one way, and contact can be lost completely.

- Gives the doctor ideas in seconds, 24/7.

- Free and open-source, with no cloud: health data never leaves the device.

- The doctor stays in charge, which keeps it safe.

- Light: it runs in a normal browser on an ordinary laptop.

INTENDED IMPACT

We want to show that a small offline AI can support crew medical autonomy on the way to Mars. Next steps: an AI that reads the photo itself, heart rate and fatigue from the camera (rPPG) as an early warning, and a photo timeline to follow healing. The same idea could help people on Earth who are far from a doctor, for example on ships, in Antarctica or in remote villages.

HOW IT IS CREATIVE

- The whole AI runs inside a browser tab: no server, no cloud, no install. You open a web page once and it keeps working offline.

- It is designed around the Mars communication delay, for the moments when Earth cannot answer in time.

- The AI's advice is grounded in NASA and medical findings about skin in space, not only general advice from Earth.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

- Safety: the AI never diagnoses and never gives medicine doses; the doctor decides. Answers are short and follow a fixed format, so they are quick to read.

- Communication: delays of 3 to 22 minutes and possible loss of contact, so everything must work offline.

- Privacy: photos and health data stay on the device.

- Limited hardware: a small 1B model in 4-bit, so it fits on an ordinary laptop's graphics card.

- Honest limits: the AI does not read the photo yet; it works from the doctor's description.

TOOLS

- Languages: C#, HTML, CSS, JavaScript

- Framework: .NET 10 Blazor WebAssembly

- AI: WebLLM (MLC AI) with Llama 3.2 1B Instruct (q4f16_1), running on WebGPU

- Hosting and build: GitHub, GitHub Actions, GitHub Pages

- Development: Visual Studio; Claude (Anthropic) as coding assistant; Gamma for the slides

- Hardware: a normal laptop or PC with a WebGPU-capable browser; no special hardware
